subject.title: Feature: Native Audio Input for Omni-Modal Models (skip STT transcription)

question: Should OpenClaw add native audio forwarding for inbound voice notes, and what raw-media egress, transcript/audit, fallback, provider-capability, and config policy should govern it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent behavior changes sensitive media egress, provider/model routing, user-facing config, and session transcript semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the product and security contract.

options.title: Design the native-audio contract first
options.body: Settle typed audio blocks, provider serialization, explicit opt-in, raw-media egress policy, fallback behavior, payload limits, and transcript/audit metadata before implementation.

options.title: Keep transcription-only for now
options.body: Leave inbound audio on the current STT transcript path until maintainers decide that raw audio forwarding is acceptable.

options.title: Adopt the open PR after rework
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78797 only after it rebases and addresses proof, contract, provider transport/auth, consumer, and security blockers.

recommendation.title: Design the native-audio contract first
recommendation.body: Settle typed audio blocks, provider serialization, explicit opt-in, raw-media egress policy, fallback behavior, payload limits, and transcript/audit metadata before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The original media pipeline and later provider/media contract history make steipete the best available routing owner for the core product/security contract decision.
